servo_hz.label: PROPOSED DESIGN

driver.label: PROPOSED DESIGN

moving_mass_kg.unit: kg (X axis; the Y axis moves 0.29 kg)
moving_mass_kg.label: CALCULATION

actuator.value: H-bot, 2 x NEMA 17 closed-loop steppers, GT2 belts, 20-tooth pulleys, miniature rails
actuator.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
actuator.source: NEMA 17 hybrid stepper 17HS19-2004S1 (ledger AMF-92: 0.59 N m holding, 2.0 A, 1.4 ohm, 3.0 mH, rotor 82 g cm2); closed-loop variant with a 1000-line encoder, e.g. StepperOnline 17E1K series (https://www.omc-stepperonline.com/nema-17-closed-loop-stepper-motor, retrieved via a search listing 2026-09-30); ADI/Trinamic TMC2209 stepper driver, StealthChop2 'no-noise' chopper (ledger AMF-93)

travel_mm.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
travel_mm.source: a whole accepted word up to about 80 mm long passes under a still pen; a line change of 2-3 lines

servo_hz.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
servo_hz.source: well below the belt ringing of desktop belt machines (Klipper resonance compensation guide: axis ringing below about 20-25 Hz calls for a stiffer frame or a lighter moving mass; example measurement 49.4 Hz; https://www.klipper3d.org/Resonance_Compensation.html (retrieved 2026-09-30))

speed_cap_mm_s.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
speed_cap_mm_s.source: accepted writing needs <= 30 mm/s (the reference limit)

choice.value: low vacuum through a perforated plate (primary), with a hinged clip bar and three edge stops for registration; a low-tack adhesive carrier sheet as the silent alternative
choice.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
choice.source: Cricut LightGrip machine mat: low-tack adhesive carrier that holds printer paper in a cutting machine; https://cricut.com/en-us/tools-accessories/machine-tools/machine-mats/lightgrip-machine-mat-12-x-12/2001976.html (retrieved 2026-09-30)

shear_capacity_N.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
shear_capacity_N.source: 3 x the largest shear the paper meets (a hand resting on the paper, about 1 N; the ball drag is 0.15-0.4 N)

registration.value: two stops on the top edge, one on the left edge; the camera reads two printed or pencilled corner marks to register the sheet to about 0.2 mm
registration.label: PROPOSED DESIGN

electroadhesion.value: not chosen: kV electrodes under the user's hand, humidity-dependent hold
electroadhesion.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
electroadhesion.source: Electroadhesion release pressures 1-100 kPa (conductive objects at 400 V; dielectric objects 1-100 x the pre-contact adhesion; ledger AMF-114)

palm_rest.value: a fixed bridge across the lower edge of the plate, padded, adjustable 15-35 mm above the paper; the hand rests on it and never touches the moving paper; the fingers reach over its front edge
palm_rest.label: PROPOSED DESIGN

primary.value: global-shutter camera (250 fps region of interest) on a side arm, tracking a small retro-reflective or IR-LED marker ring within 3 mm of the ball; the same camera reads the sheet's registration marks
primary.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
primary.source: InnoMaker global-shutter camera modules for Raspberry Pi: OV9281 1280x800 at 120 fps (144 fps with the maker's driver), 640x400 at 253 fps; https://www.inno-maker.com/gs-camera/ (retrieved 2026-09-30)

alternative.value: EMR digitiser under the non-metallic plate, with an EMR ink pen; actuators kept outside its active area
alternative.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
alternative.source: Wacom EMR OEM digitiser boards (ledger AMF-98): resolution 0.01 mm, accuracy +-0.4 mm, reading height 5-14 mm, 133 points/s; Cintiq 12WX (ledger CON-84): +-0.5 mm, 133 points/s; Intuos Pro Paper Edition with ink pens on A5/A4 paper (ledger OPT-86); tablet digitisers about 200 Hz (ledger OPT-03)

contact.value: three load cells under the plate: pen normal force at 1 kHz; contact on above 50 mN
contact.label: PROPOSED DESIGN

pen_imu.value: for free writing: the pen's IMU (clip-on on an ordinary pen, or built into a light stylus), wired or 2.4 GHz proprietary radio (BLE adds 7.5-15 ms)
pen_imu.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
pen_imu.source: TDK ICM-42688-P accelerometer noise 70 ug/sqrt(Hz) (ledger OPT-39); ST LSM6DSV16X 60 ug/sqrt(Hz) (OPT-37); study E's IMU budget: anti-aliasing 1.04 ms + FIFO/SPI 0.35 ms + pair averaging 0.13 ms = 1.52 ms (docs/readable_target.md section 6); Bluetooth LE: minimum connection interval 7.5 ms, reduced to 375 us by Core 6.2's Shorter Connection Intervals (https://www.bluetooth.com/bluetooth-core-6-2-feature-overview/, retrieved 2026-09-30; proposed row AMF-287)

choice.value: Z-drop of the paper plate by 3 mm (three push-pull solenoids on a flexure, or one voice coil); the user keeps the pen down; the load cells confirm the break before any air move
choice.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
choice.source: Plotter pen lift by solenoid, 0.5-0.64 mm axial (CalComp patent, ledger PAT-41)

drop_s.label: ASSUMPTION
drop_s.source: break of contact after the command; the gravity drop alone takes 25 ms (CALC, z_drop())

drop_mm.label: PROPOSED DESIGN
drop_mm.source: exceeds the fingers' assumed 1-2 mm compliance at 1 N (ASSUMPTION)

sensing_options.measures: pen acceleration and rotation (no absolute position)
sensing_options.delay_ms: 1.5 (study E's IMU path: anti-aliasing + FIFO + averaging) + link: 1-2 wired or proprietary radio, 7.5-15 with BLE
sensing_options.noise: accelerometer 60-70 µg/√Hz (OPT-37, OPT-39); tremor-band position from the IMU alone about 0.29 mm with a linear filter on the tremor alone (study F)
sensing_options.pros: any pen the user likes; cheap
sensing_options.cons: no position: cannot write accepted text alone; clip adds 5-8 g off-axis; BLE latency
sensing_options.label: MANUFACTURER / LITERATURE (ledger ids) and ASSUMPTION (link)

sensing_options.option: Light stylus with IMU + contact (force) sensing
sensing_options.measures: acceleration, rotation, refill force (contact) at 1 kHz
sensing_options.noise: as the IMU; contact force about 10 mN (ASSUMPTION)
sensing_options.pros: known geometry and mass; contact known at the tip
sensing_options.cons: not the user's own pen; still no absolute position
sensing_options.label: ASSUMPTION on the IMU data above

sensing_options.option: Tip tracking by an overhead or side camera
sensing_options.measures: marker position near the tip in the desk frame (absolute, drift-free) and the sheet's marks
sensing_options.delay_ms: 4-8 (exposure + readout + processing; OptiTrack-class 4.2 at 240 fps, MANUFACTURER)
sensing_options.noise: 10-20 um RMS per axis with sub-pixel centroiding at about 0.1 mm per pixel (ASSUMPTION)
sensing_options.pros: absolute; works with any pen fitted with a marker; also registers the sheet
sensing_options.cons: occlusion by the fingers from above (a side arm is better); the marker sits above the ball, so pen rotation reads as motion (kappa, part c)
sensing_options.label: MANUFACTURER (frame rates, latency) and ASSUMPTION (noise)

sensing_options.option: Sensing through the platen (EMR digitiser under a non-metallic plate)
sensing_options.measures: EMR pen coil position, pressure and tilt, absolute
sensing_options.delay_ms: 7.5-15 (one or two reports at 133-266 points/s + USB; ASSUMPTION on the reported rates)
sensing_options.noise: resolution 0.01 mm; accuracy +-0.4-0.5 mm absolute (AMF-98, CON-84); jitter 10-50 um (ASSUMPTION)
sensing_options.pros: no line of sight; pressure gives contact; proven with ink pens on paper (OPT-86)
sensing_options.cons: needs an EMR pen; the coil is 5-10 mm above the ball (tilt error unless corrected with the reported tilt); metal and magnets of the stage distort the field; lower rate and higher delay than a camera
sensing_options.label: MANUFACTURER / LITERATURE (ledger ids) and ASSUMPTION
